title: Hypernormalisation: find the seam in the sealed room

card.name: The Sealed Room
card.lore: Hypernormalisation is treating fakeness as normal because alternatives seem unimaginable.
card.power: Present the system as total, with absolutely no outside to step into.

visual.value: Style: surrealist editorial. Subject: total system with all exits bricked over, fakeness labeled as reality. Mood: hypernormalized enclosure.
visual.inspection: Printed: the figure holds a cane inside a box lined with repeated city skylines. The line draws on the skyline and cane.

interpretation.summary: In the late Soviet sequence Curtis describes economic planning sustained by public pretence. At 00:24:08–00:24:29 he links playing along to the difficulty of imagining an alternative and names hypernormalisation. This is the narrator’s historical interpretation.
interpretation.counterposition: Ask which concrete institution, decision and alternative the account identifies. A claim of no outside must be tested against specific cases.

brainfood.text: Nice skyline. Same rent on all four walls? Hand me that cane. I’d like to tap one of those buildings.
brainfood.spokenDE: Schicke Skyline. Auf allen vier Wänden dieselbe Miete? Gib mir mal den Stock. Ich würd gern gegen eins von den Häusern klopfen.
